ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a pie chart, and the percentages are directly marked on the five sectors, respectively 47%, 24%, 12%, 11%, and 6%. Then reason: Let the population percentages of the five regions, center, north, west, east, and south, respectively be C, N, W, E, S. The problem gives C = N + W + E, and S = W/2. The total is 100%, so C + N + W + E + S = 100. Since N + W + E = C, we can get 2C + S = 100. Observing the values in the pie chart, 47% and 6% satisfy 2×47% + 6% = 100%, so C = 47%, S = 6%. Also because S = W/2, W = 12%. The remaining two sectors, 11% and 24%, correspond to the north region and the east region, so the difference between the population percentages of the north region and the east region is 24% - 11% = 13%.

method.method_draft: Read the pie chart sectors as 47%, 24%, 12%, 11%, and 6%. From the text, let C, N, W, E, S be the central, north, west, east, and south zone percentages. Use C = N + W + E and S = W/2, with all five zone values being the five visible pie sectors. Since the total is 100%, C + N + W + E + S = 100 and N + W + E = C, so 2C + S = 100. Test the visible sector values: C = 47 and S = 6 satisfy 2·47 + 6 = 100. Then W = 12. The remaining visible sectors, 11% and 24%, must be north and east, so their percentage difference is 24% - 11% = 13%.

method.method_draft: Read the pie chart as five unlabeled slices: 47%, 24%, 12%, 11%, and 6%. Start from the text condition that the south zone has half the inhabitants of the west zone, so west and south must be two visible slices in a 2:1 ratio.
